newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: New Lithuania economy chief backs wider sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: New Lithuania economy chief backs wider sell-offs.

text.p: Lithuania's new economy minister Vincas Babilius said on Friday he favoured expanding the list of companies that were on the list for privatisation and favoured some private capital in firms that were considered strategic industries.
Babilius, 59, was earlier named as head of a new enlarged economy minister by Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius.
He is the deputy head of the Confederation of Industrialists and director of a firm which makes electric measuring equipment.
He said he wanted parliament to review the list of companies that were currently banned from sale because they were considered strategic to state interests.
"Of course the state should keep in its hands strategic companies but we should not be afraid of privatisation," Babilius told Reuters in an interview.
Stategic firms are usually considered to be the energy companies, railways and the nuclear power plant, Ignalina. Babilius said he wanted to cut the number of firms on the list.
"It is necessary to review this list, especially in the energy sphere," Babilius added.
He said that even with companies like Ignalina, government control did not have to be total.
"Every company has a possible owner and the state should not attempt to own but to regulate," Babilius said.
"Of course the state must control (strategic companies) but that does not mean that it should contol 100 percent of the company. It can maintain control with less shares," he added.

Lithuania is seen as a laggard in the race to attract private capital and foreign investment although the outgoing government of former communists did stabilise the economy after the country's split from the former Soviet Union.
